comments.text: The problem is that in Slovenia we have selfish, obedient globalist servants in power on both the left and the right, so unfortunately, despite all the exceptional natural resources, we are not a sovereign country.

comments.author: @nexttrip88
comments.text: The emphasis on community and slow, intentional living in Slovenia is so refreshing. It’s inspiring to see a small nation stay so connected to its roots and landscapes

comments.author: @thomascarey2941
comments.text: While this tour is beautifully done, there are severe omissions: Present a map and the major places first and often because most North Americans could not identify Slovenia on a European map; present a more studied relationship of Slovenia on the Balkan Peninsula with neighboring countries; discuss the dominant language in much greater detail. I have heard Slovenian in America and it reminds me of Serbo-Croatian; discuss the dominant religion (Orthodox?)
